question.value: How do the EHV jet and slow outflow interact (outflow force content), and what is the chemical composition and spatial location of molecules in the slow wing, fast wing and EHV jet of Serpens Main outflows?

evidence.quote: The first aim is to analyze the interaction between the EHV jet and the slow outflow by comparing their outflow force content.
The second aim is to analyze the chemical composition of the different outflow velocity components and to reveal the spatial location of molecules.

analysis_steps.goal: Column densities and abundances relative to CO

method.value: Optically thin LTE column density per pixel integrated over each velocity regime; average over pixels >3 sigma in hand-defined regions; abundance = N(X)/N(CO)

evidence.quote: the average of the column density within the pre-defined region is calculated from only those pixels with signal above 3 $\sigma$.

findings_qualitative.value: SiO abundance generally enhanced with velocity; HCN in slow and fast wings but absent in EHV; H2CO mostly low velocity but in one Ser-emb 8 (N) EHV bullet

evidence.quote: The SiO abundance is generally enhanced with velocity, while HCN is present in the slow and the fast wing, but disappears in the EHV jet.

findings_qualitative.value: No complex organic molecules associated with outflows

evidence.quote: No complex organic molecules are found to be associated with the outflows.

claims.hypothesis: Is the EHV jet able to power the slow outflow?
claims.experiment: Outflow force per velocity regime from CO 2-1
claims.result: EHV share 5-40%; exceeds wings only for blue Ser-emb 8 (N)
claims.finding: EHV jet generally lacks enough force; only Ser-emb 8 (N) has enough momentum

evidence.quote: only the EHV jet in the youngest source Ser-emb 8 (N) has enough momentum to power the slow outflow.

claims.finding: EHV jets may be more common than thought

evidence.quote: The high detection rate suggests that the presence of the EHV jet may be more common than previously expected.

claims.hypothesis: Does the chemistry differ between velocity components?
claims.experiment: Abundances relative to CO for SiO, H2CO, HCN by regime
claims.result: SiO rises with velocity, HCN absent in EHV
claims.finding: Consistent with low C/O in EHV gas

evidence.quote: The data are consistent with a low C/O ratio in the EHV gas versus high C/O ratio in the fast and slow wings.

why_this_method.value: Single transition per molecule so Tex assumed (CO 75 K; others via RADEX range)

evidence.quote: Since only a single transition of each molecule was observed, it is not possible to derive an excitation temperature from these data.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Higher excitation temperatures in fast wing and EHV (250/300/700 K) tested; does not change SMM1-a picture but changes SMM1-b and Ser-emb 8 (N)

evidence.quote: For the case of SMM1-a, it does not change the general picture of the EHV jet contributing only a small fraction of the outflow force.
